headline: Berkeley has already modelled this. BeTH reuses the City's StreetSaver-based projections rather than building a rival model, and adds the funding-restriction test the City does not publish.
chain: network PCI over time (City deterioration model)

pci60_assessment.question: What would it take to bring Berkeley pavement to PCI 60 or better and hold it there?
pci60_assessment.answer_status: ANSWERABLE FROM CITY DATA, with limits stated
pci60_assessment.finding: The City's own 12-year projections bracket PCI 60. The Five-Year Plan alone is projected to DECLINE to about 56 by 2038. Adding Measure FF is projected to reach about 62 by 2038. So PCI 60+ is, on the City's own modelling, roughly the outcome already purchased by the Plan plus Measure FF, at about $29.6 million a year.
pci60_assessment.the_real_gap_is_70_not_60: Berkeley's adopted goal is PCI 70 (BMC 7.11.010(K)(1)), not 60. The City estimates PCI 70 by 2036 requires about $37.6 million a year, roughly $8 million a year more than current plans provide. The funding question Berkeley actually faces is the 62-to-70 gap.

scenarios_below_60.label: Five-Year Plan baseline
scenarios_below_60.description: Only the funding in the proposed Five-Year Street Rehabilitation Plan. PCI falls from 59 to about 56 by 2038 as construction cost escalation outpaces revenue growth.
scenarios_below_60.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

scenarios_at_or_above_60.label: Five-Year Plan + Measure FF
scenarios_at_or_above_60.description: Adds Measure FF funding. PCI improves from 59 to about 62 by 2038. Measure FF accounts for the entire difference between this and the baseline.
scenarios_at_or_above_60.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

scenarios_at_or_above_60.label: Reach 70 by 2036, then maintain
scenarios_at_or_above_60.description: The investment level the City estimates is needed to reach PCI 70 by 2036 and hold it through 2038. About $8M a year more than the Plan and Measure FF currently provide.
scenarios_at_or_above_60.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

critical_caveats: These are the CITY's projections, not BeTH's. BeTH has not independently verified them and cannot, without the StreetSaver segment data.

PCI 60 as a network AVERAGE can coexist with many streets in failed condition. The City's own goal pairs PCI 70 with "no streets having a PCI below 50". A network average target without a distribution floor can be met while the worst streets decay further.
All figures assume 3% annual construction cost escalation and the Council/Measure FF revenue escalation formulas. The City notes the net effect is a modest real increase in costs relative to funding.
Annual figures are 12-year averages accounting for projected revenue growth, NOT flat annual amounts.
Reaching a level and holding it are different problems with different funding profiles.
pci60_assessment.what_beth_adds: Not a rival forecast. BeTH's contribution is to show what the City's own model implies under alternative funding, and to test whether any capital reallocation could close the roughly $8M/yr gap to PCI 70. That test is currently blocked: 0 of 15 CIP funding sources are confirmed redirectable.

current_network_pci.note: Citywide PCI as of the most recent condition assessment (2025).

assessment_cycle.note: PCI scored per street section from observed surface distresses, fed into StreetSaver.

adopted_goal.source: BMC 7.11.010(K)(1), via City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)
adopted_goal.note: Goal of citywide PCI 70 "ideally with no streets having a PCI below 50". Measure FF prioritises streets below PCI 50.

total_lane_miles.needed_from: StreetSaver network summary. Not required for the City-scenario comparison, only for independent segment modelling.

pci_distribution.needed_from: StreetSaver segment export. Needed to report miles below PCI 25 and the condition distribution.

deterioration.note: Deterioration is non-linear. Below roughly PCI 40 the required treatment escalates from surface seal to full reconstruction at several times the cost. A linear assumption makes PCI 60 look far cheaper to reach than it is, so no linear fallback is provided.

catalog.needed_from: StreetSaver treatment catalog: eligibility PCI band, unit cost per square foot, service life, post-treatment PCI

treatments.note: Treatment eligibility depends on current PCI. A treatment valid at PCI 70 is usually invalid at PCI 35.

cost_decomposition.needed_from: Contract bid tabs, broken into pavement treatment, design, construction management, ADA, utilities, drainage, traffic safety, environmental work, green infrastructure, discretionary scope

delivery_cost.note: Whether delivery reform frees real money can only be answered from this decomposition. Do not presume environmental review is the primary driver; that is the hypothesis to test.

measure_ff_annual_estimate.source: City of Berkeley, Proposed FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Program presentation, Item 02
measure_ff_annual_estimate.note: NOT all pavement: the same sentence covers sidewalks, safety and environment. Not usable as a paving budget without the split.

redirectable_from_capital.needed_from: Restriction research across CIP funding sources. 0 of 15 sources currently confirmed redirectable.

construction_cost_pct_per_year.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)
construction_cost_pct_per_year.note: Reflects recent asphalt and paving material trends.

revenue_escalation.value: greater of SF Bay Area cost of living or California per capita personal income growth
revenue_escalation.source: Council Resolution No. 70,456-N.S. and the Measure FF ordinance, via City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

net_effect_stated_by_city.value: a modest real increase in construction costs relative to available funding over the projection period
net_effect_stated_by_city.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

independent_model_status.purpose: Segment-level modelling would let BeTH test the City's projections rather than only restate them, and report the condition DISTRIBUTION the City's headline average hides.

missing_inputs.needed_from: StreetSaver network summary. Not required for the City-scenario comparison, only for independent segment modelling.
StreetSaver segment export. Needed to report miles below PCI 25 and the condition distribution.
StreetSaver treatment catalog: eligibility PCI band, unit cost per square foot, service life, post-treatment PCI

independent_model_status.rule: No default, literature or assumed value is ever substituted for a missing input.

reconciliation_requirement: BeTH figures must reconcile to the City's adopted paving plan and StreetSaver output, with differences explained.
